<description>
**Problem:** Binary GET and POST requests to `/rest/getutxos` for the same outpoints should agree. GET finds the unspent output, but POST incorrectly reports no hit.
The POST decoder writes the body into a `DataStream` with `operator<<`, serializing it as a string and prepending a CompactSize length. It then reads the first byte of that added length as the checkmempool flag, misaligning the later request fields. Hex POST bodies use the same decoding and are affected too.

**Fix:** Deserialize the supplied body bytes directly. Separate commits apply the existing 15-outpoint limit during decoding before allocating the vector, and use `SpanReader` to avoid the extra copy into a `DataStream`.
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6397174832 comment by fametrano (contributor):
tACK b7622767c6e4100ea2d0ac8fae2d6c98a43d081d

I sent 14 POST bodies, each in binary and in hex, to regtest nodes built at the merge base and at this head, and compared each answer with the binary GET for the same outpoints, or with a 400 where a library I maintain rejects the body. The head matches on all 28 requests and the base on 10. The new test fails on the base at the GET/POST comparison.

A POST body that names no outpoints gets a 200 with an empty result. A URI without outpoints and an empty body get "Error: empty request". The body `01 00` (checkmempool, no outpoints) was a 400 on the base only because of the misread length. A hex body of only whitespace, such as `" "`, is a 200 on both. Adding `if (vOutPoints.empty()) return RESTERR(req, HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, "Error: empty request");` before the max-outpoints check makes these a 400 too. With `01 00` and `" "` added to `interface_rest.py`, the test passes with the line and fails without it. I can share the harness.
</new_statements>
